reader_question: How many residents per 100,000 does each state hold in prison?
grade_line: Documented: counts the states report to the Bureau of Justice Statistics
title: State imprisonment rates at the end of 2023 ran from 96 sentenced prisoners per 100,000 residents in Massachusetts to 652 in Mississippi.
measure_line: Imprisonment rate: prisoners serving sentences of more than one year under each state’s authority, per 100,000 state residents, December 31, 2023, 50 states.
notes: The card shows each state as a dot, ranked from the highest rate to the lowest, and labels only the two states in the title; the table below gives every state’s rate, as Rule 14.18’s dot plot does.
alt: Dots for the 50 states’ imprisonment rates at the end of 2023, highest at the left, beside a dashed line for all states together at 318 per 100,000. Mississippi held the most, 652 per 100,000 residents, and Massachusetts the fewest, 96.

words.b: Prisons and jails form one system; includes jail populations
words.c: Leaves out its own prisoners held in federal or other states’ prisons
words.d: Includes a few sentences of one year or less
words.d,f: Includes a few sentences of one year or less, and people serving 1 to 2.5 years in local jails
words.e: Includes people waiting in county jail to move to a state prison
words.g: Leaves out people in residential confinement

chart_notes: The dashed line marks all states together, 318 per 100,000. Open dots mark the six states whose prisons and jails form one system.

labels.key_open: Prisons and jails form one system, so the rate includes jail populations
labels.card_source: Every state’s rate: Bureau of Justice Statistics, Prisoners in 2023, Table 7. Chart: Oath & Action
labels.card_note: Each dot is a state, highest at the left.

card.post: State imprisonment rates at the end of 2023 ran from 96 sentenced prisoners per 100,000 residents in Massachusetts to 652 in Mississippi. All states together held 318 per 100,000. The Bureau of Justice Statistics’ Prisoners in 2023, Table 7, gives every state’s rate.
